title: Regional failover UX + customer notifications: Console messaging, status page alignment, and comms rules
creator: Paula Mendes
project: Regional Failover Automation Upgrade (Reliability Program Q1–Q2 2026)
description:
Define customer-facing expectations for automated/assisted regional failover across Hosted API + Dedicated. This includes: (1) what customers see in the Redwood Console during impairment and failover, (2) how status page updates align with what Console shows, and (3) what notifications (if any) are sent to customers during both real regional incidents and planned controlled failover tests (“game days”).

Why now
- We are increasing automation in regional failover (trigger pipeline, deterministic policy evaluation, rollback guardrails). We need consistent customer-facing behavior to avoid confusion, reduce support load, and set the right reliability expectations.
- The Q1 2026 controlled failover tests surfaced gaps: customers saw transient errors and had no clear in-product context; status-page messaging lagged behind what internal tooling showed; Support needed a consistent explanation of multi-region behavior.

Goals
- Customers have clear, accurate, non-alarming messaging in Console during: regional impairment, planned tests, failover in progress, and recovery/rollback.
- Status page messaging is consistent with Console, and both are sourced from the same underlying “event state” where possible.
- Notifications are predictable and opt-in where appropriate, with explicit policies by tier (self-serve vs enterprise; Hosted vs Dedicated).

Non-goals
- Changing contract/SLA language (tracked separately).
- Building a fully customizable per-customer notification system in this phase.
- Providing per-request routing traces to customers (internal-only for now).

Definitions / event taxonomy (customer-facing)
- Planned controlled failover test: Redwood-initiated test with guardrails and limited blast radius.
- Regional impairment: Redwood-identified degradation affecting a cloud region (reachability and/or elevated errors/latency/capacity) that may trigger traffic shifting.
- Failover in progress: active traffic steering away from an impaired region to an alternate region for impacted traffic.
- Degraded performance: service is operating but may have elevated tail latency, higher retry rates, or partial feature impact (e.g., streaming disconnect risk).

Customer-facing surfaces
A) Redwood Console (customer UI)
1) Global banner (org-level)
- Visible to all users in the org when Redwood declares an incident OR when automation is actively shifting traffic that could affect that org’s requests.
- Should not enumerate internal signal names (“burn rate”, “reachability probes”); should communicate effect + recommended actions.

2) Status widget (per project / per route / per model where applicable)
- A lightweight indicator with state: Normal | Degraded | Failover in progress | Recovered.
- If Dedicated: also show “Dedicated capacity: normal/degraded” based on pool drain/failover workflow states.

3) Incident timeline link-out
- Link to status page incident entry when public.
- If not public (e.g., micro-event below threshold), Console can show “We are investigating elevated errors in <region>” without creating a public incident. Must align with internal comms policy below.

B) Status page (public)
- Must distinguish planned test vs real incident.
- Must not imply customer action is required unless we have a clear recommendation.
- Update cadence requirements below.

C) Notifications (email/webhook/in-app)
- Default: no new proactive notifications for self-serve customers beyond Console + status page.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: targeted comms for planned tests and for meaningful incidents when configured.

Messaging rules (Console)
- Banner copy states (draft requirements)
1) Planned test window
  - Title: “Planned reliability test: regional failover”
  - Body: “We’re running a controlled regional failover test to validate reliability. Some requests may see brief retries or elevated latency. We’re monitoring closely.”
  - CTA: link to status page planned maintenance entry (or dedicated planned test page) + link to docs for recommended retry/backoff.

2) Degraded performance (no active failover)
  - Title: “Degraded performance in <region>”
  - Body: “We’re seeing elevated error rates/latency. Traffic is not currently shifting. We’re mitigating.”
  - CTA: status page incident if public, otherwise “Learn more” linking to a help article explaining multi-region behavior and what customers can do (idempotency keys, retry-after handling).

3) Failover in progress
  - Title: “Traffic shifting to maintain availability”
  - Body: “We’re redirecting traffic from <region A> to <region B> to maintain service. You may see brief elevated latency or reconnects for streaming.”
  - CTA: link to status page + link to client guidance (streaming reconnect + idempotency).

4) Recovery / rollback
  - Title: “Service stabilizing”
  - Body: “Traffic shifting is complete. We’re continuing to monitor.”
  - Auto-dismiss criteria: after 30 minutes stable + no customer-impacting alert firing, or when incident is resolved.

Console scope/segmentation
- Show banners to:
  - Hosted API: orgs that sent >N requests in last 30 minutes to impacted routing tier/region pair OR are currently routed away from primary.
  - Dedicated: orgs whose dedicated pool is involved in drain/evacuation or whose overflow policy is active.
- Avoid showing a global banner to unrelated tenants to prevent confusion.

Status page policy (what gets posted)
- Planned controlled tests
  - Post a planned maintenance entry (or dedicated “planned test” template) at least 24 hours before the window.
  - Include: start/end window, what may be impacted (brief retries/latency), and how we’ll monitor.
  - Provide explicit “What you need to do: nothing” unless we have a required action.

- Real incidents
  - Post when there is a meaningful customer-impacting regional event (e.g., multi-region availability SLO burn threshold, or sustained elevated 5xx/timeouts across multiple routes) AND on-call declares an incident.
  - Updates:
    - First update within 10 minutes of incident declaration.
    - Subsequent updates every 30 minutes during active mitigation, or sooner if state changes (failover started/complete/rolled back).

Notifications policy
1) Self-serve (Hosted API)
- No proactive email by default.
- Customers discover via Console banner + status page.

2) Enterprise (Hosted API)
- For SEV-1/SEV-2 incidents: send email to configured incident contacts (existing mechanism) with link to status page + brief summary.
- No new “per failover action” notifications (avoid noise). The email should reflect incident severity/state.

3) Dedicated customers
- Planned tests: proactive email to named customer contacts (CS owns list), at least 48 hours in advance for tests that could touch dedicated routing/drain workflows.
- Real incidents: CS-led targeted comms if impact is expected >5 minutes or if dedicated capacity is being drained/failed over.

4) Webhooks
- Not in scope for this phase unless we can reuse existing incident webhook infrastructure. (Open question: do we already have a customer-facing webhook for status page events?)

Comms ownership and approvals
- Console banner: Product defines copy; Design signs off; SRE approves runtime correctness (don’t overpromise); Support approves “what should customers do” guidance.
- Status page updates: SRE on-call owns; comms playbook defines who approves external language for SEV-1 (SRE lead + Support liaison).
- Planned test announcement: SRE program lead + PM approval before posting.

Telemetry / integration requirements (inputs)
- Console must be driven by automation events + region health state, not manual copy/paste.
- Required signals for UI state:
  - “failover_event” audit events (recommended/executed/rolled_back) with region pair + tier + affected routing group.
  - Region health state (Normal/Degraded/Impaired) from region health aggregator.
  - Dedicated drain workflow state + progress metrics.
- Avoid exposing tenant identifiers on public status page; internal mapping stays internal.

Acceptance criteria
- Console has defined states + copy, and engineering can implement without further PM decisions.
- Status page template language exists for:
  - Planned controlled failover test
  - Regional impairment with failover in progress
  - Regional impairment without failover
- Documented policy exists for when we do/don’t notify customers directly, by tier.
- Support has a short “FAQ / explanation” snippet for inbound tickets (multi-region behavior, expected client retry behavior, streaming reconnect guidance).

Links
- Status page templates: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/status-page-template-regional-event.json
- Comms playbook: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json
- Console banner mock: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/failover-console-banner-mock.json
- Design tickets: DES-187, DES-188
- Multi-region SLO context: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json

Open questions
- Do we want customers to see the specific destination region during failover (e.g., “us-east -> eu-west”)? Proposed: yes in Console (for transparency), no on status page (keep general) unless it materially affects performance.
- For data residency constrained accounts: should Console avoid showing alternate region names if the account is pinned? Proposed: still show “traffic shifting” only if shifting is possible; otherwise show “degraded in-region; failover not available for this configuration.” Need Security/Compliance review.
- How do we handle partial impairment limited to a model family (e.g., only one GPU pool type)? Proposed: per-route/model widget shows “Degraded” but global banner only if org impact crosses threshold.

Risks
- Over-notifying creates noise and churn; under-notifying creates support spikes and customer distrust.
- Copy that suggests a customer action (retry/backoff) must match actual gateway behavior (retry-after semantics, idempotency support). Coordinate with gateway/circuit breaker owners.

Next steps
- Finalize copy + state machine with Design (DES-187) and status page copy (DES-188).
- Confirm event sourcing from audit logs (ENG-2424/ENG-2418 related) and incident-bot summaries.
- Produce a Support-ready FAQ snippet and add to comms playbook.
comments: 2026-01-08 — Paula Mendes: Created ticket after kickoff; need firm decisions before 1/15 controlled failover. Primary pain: customers saw 5xx and asked Support with no in-product context.

2026-01-09 — Devon Price (Incident-bot/tooling): We can emit concise failover summaries into internal incident channels already. For Console, we need a stable event schema (failover_event.audit) and a way to query “current effective routing state” per org to avoid showing banners to everyone.

2026-01-10 — Lauren Bishop (Dedicated product): Dedicated customers will ask “are you draining my pool?”—we need a dedicated-specific widget state. Also, planned tests touching Dedicated require proactive comms; CS already has contact lists but needs lead time.

2026-01-12 — Owen Phillips (Support incident liaison): Strong preference: don’t add default emails for self-serve. Console banner + status page is enough; we can template replies for tickets. We should explicitly say “no action needed” for planned tests.

2026-01-14 — Nora Ahmed (Customer status UX): From a UX standpoint, “Failover in progress” should be a distinct state, but we should avoid region jargon in the primary message. Region detail can be behind “Details” expansion. Will align with DES-187.

2026-01-16 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): During the game day we had a window where traffic was shifting but status page still showed “investigating.” We need a rule: when automation executes a policy flip affecting >X% traffic, status page update should reflect “traffic shifting.”

2026-01-17 — Victor Alvarez (Network): Please avoid attributing blame (“cloud provider outage”) in customer copy unless confirmed. Use “network connectivity issues in <region>” only when reachability probes confirm and SRE has declared incident.

2026-01-21 — Marissa Cole (Rollback/workflow PM): Copy must cover rollback too. Customers noticed a ‘flip-flop’ pattern in staging; we should message rollback as “stabilizing” rather than implying failure of automation.

2026-01-28 — Nikhil Sharma: Drafted notification policy by tier in description. Remaining: confirm enterprise email mechanism scope (existing incident contact emails) and whether status page planned maintenance supports “controlled test” labeling cleanly.

2026-02-04 — Kira Thompson (Runbooks/docs): Once finalized, I’ll add the FAQ snippet to the comms playbook and make sure it matches the Hosted API failover runbook language (no contradictory guidance on retries/streaming reconnect).
